novelty_flags.label: Theorem 2 — sharp-stage frontier
novelty_flags.one_line: The main result needs an explicit comparison with classical c-estimability/c-optimal polynomial-regression design work (for example Elfving 1952, Kiefer–Wolfowitz 1959, and Studden 1968), which is a closer mathematical comparator than the current two-paper rollout contrast.

novelty_flags.label: Related work — XiongAtheyBayatiImbens2023 comparison
novelty_flags.one_line: The text attributes a five-stage treated-fraction path to Theorem 3.1, but the published theorem gives T-period GLS optimality conditions; its displayed examples and S-shape are not a five-measured-stage theorem.

source_verification_receipts.version: Management Science 70(8), 2024, pp. 5317–5336; publisher PDF updated December 27, 2024
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.1 gives conditions for a T-optimal irreversible GLS design under its stated model and T-dependent condition; the paper describes S-shaped treated fractions but does not state a five-measured-stage schedule theorem.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the Xiong description with its precise T-period GLS optimality claim and add a compact comparison against classical c-estimability/c-optimal polynomial-regression design theory, identifying exactly which monotone shifted-lag constraint defeats each generic result.

Remove the homogeneous boundary proposition as a standalone target and replace it with a nontrivial robustness result, such as an explicit bias formula or sensitivity bound for degree-(r+1) trend leakage.

Make the exact-risk component non-routine by posing a genuine schedule-placement result under the shared-hash kernel—such as a computable optimum or strict separation from diagonal GLS—rather than retaining only the covariance expansion and KKT system.

recommended_next_step: Revise the literature positioning and remove the vacuous boundary corollary; retain the conditional sharp support frontier as the field-level kernel and demote duplicated covariance/KKT material to supporting context.
